sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Fonts, colours and style scanning
sections.what: Sets three font families for body text, display text and code. Also defines colour names such as ink, paper, grey and line, which read CSS variables so the colours can change between light and dark modes. Tells Tailwind which source files to scan for class names.
sections.why: Likely reason: one set of style names works in both light and dark modes. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The colours depend on CSS variables defined elsewhere. A missing variable makes that colour fail silently.

summary: Sets the fonts, colour names and file scanning rules that Tailwind CSS uses to build the site's styles.
purpose: Defines the design vocabulary, so a class name such as text ink or bg paper maps to the right colour.
why: Likely reason: colours come from CSS variables so light and dark modes can swap values. Reason not stated in the code.
how: A small helper builds colour references from named CSS variables. The config then sets three font families, the colour names, a letter-spacing value, and the folders to scan.
inputs: Source files under src are scanned for class names. CSS variables are read from stylesheets elsewhere.
outputs: Generated CSS classes for fonts, colours and spacing.
risks: A colour refers to a CSS variable defined elsewhere. If that variable is missing, the colour fails without an error.
debug: If a colour does not appear, check the matching CSS variable exists and that the file using the class is inside the scanned folder.
